title: Contains Duplicate
summary: You get a list of integers `nums` in no particular order. Decide whether any value appears more than once in it: return `true` if some value repeats, and `false` if every value is different. The copies of a repeated value can sit anywhere in the list, not only side by side.

examples.explanation: 1 appears at index 1 and again at index 4, with other values in between.

approaches.twist: Keep a set of the numbers seen so far, and return true as soon as a number is already in it.
Compare every pair of numbers, and return true when two of them are equal.
approaches.note: Works with O(1) extra space, but comparing every pair takes O(n²) time. The target is O(n).

approaches.twist: Sort the numbers so equal values end up side by side, then compare each number with the next one.
approaches.note: Works with little extra space if you sort in place, but sorting takes O(n log n) time. The target is O(n).

signals.meaning: A repeat is a value you have already met. Keep the values you pass in a set, and check each new one against it before adding it.
Copies can sit far apart, so comparing neighbors misses them unless you sort first, which costs O(n log n). A set of the values seen so far catches a repeat wherever it is.
All different means a set of the values is exactly as long as the list, so comparing len(set(nums)) with len(nums) settles it too.

constraintReading: len(nums) can reach 10⁵, so comparing every pair means about 5·10⁹ checks: O(n²) is far too slow. Sorting first brings it down to O(n log n). The O(n) time target asks for one pass with O(1) set lookups, paid for with O(n) space.

related.relation: Same one pass with a memory of the values so far, but each number looks up the partner it needs instead of a copy of itself.
Also spots a repeat with a set of what it has seen, but only inside a window that slides forward.
